set.st: Late May 1898: on the road back from Holy Hill, about 4 mi from Hartford, a man shot his companion, emptied his money bag (sworn at $1,028 in gold, silver, paper and change), dragged him down a slope and drove on to Hartford. He was arrested that night with $5.75; the bag and revolver were never found. Private farmland: permission. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself. Local papers of 1898-99 cover the shooting, the bail hearing and the conviction (assault and battery: six months and a $100 fine, Apr 1899), and none reports the money recovered. A week after the shooting the Watertown Republican (8 Jun 1898) said 'the general opinion' was that the money was hidden by the assailant in the woods and the revolver thrown away; the Wisconsin Weekly Advocate (4 Jun 1898) also says 'no trace of the money' was found. At the hearing (Milwaukee Sentinel, 7 Jun 1898) it came out that on the drive back from Holy Hill the assailant left the victim, a Milwaukee man, alone in the rig 'quite a while' at a lonely spot on the Holy Hill-Hartford road before shooting him; bail was set at $5,000. The Kewaskum Statesman (4 Jun 1898) gives the assailant's statement that the victim had only $80 on him; the $1,028 (elsewhere $1,125) is the victim's own claim, and the '$5,000 bonds' in one report was the bail, not money carried. It says the assailant 'went into the woods' at the stop. Milwaukee County paid $86.25 of the victim's medical costs (West Bend News, 6 Dec 1899, p. 3); the assailant, a 'model prisoner', was released 1 Apr 1900 (Hartford Times, 8 Mar 1900, p. 3). No paper 1898-1900 reports the money bag or revolver found. The victim's brother told the same paper (2 Jun 1898, 'Did Not Have Much Money') that he doubted he ever had so much; his small grocery had been worth no more than $200-300.
